land.text: Sinop and the Black Sea coast eastward, in Rum's hands since the Seljuk capture of 1214

predecessors.note: The Sinop page: the Seljuk Turks of Rûm took the city in 1214, it returned to Trapezuntine rule briefly in 1254 and 'to Turkish control in 1265'; 'After 1265, Sinop became home to two successive independent emirates', the Pervâne and the Isfendiyars. The beyliks table dates the Pervâneid state 1277-1322.

land.text: Sinop, 'formerly ruled by the descendants of Mu'in al-Din Suleyman', annexed by Süleyman I of the Candar dynasty

successors.note: The Candar page says that after Yaman Candar's death his son Süleyman I conquered Kastamonu 'and annexed Safranbolu and Sinop, formerly ruled by the descendants of Mu'in al-Din Suleyman', without a date. Cliopatria draws the area inside its Kastamonu row from 1333 (and in the Isfendiyar row from 1344). Cliopatria's Isfendiyar row is the Candar state itself (same Wikipedia article), and its Kastamonu row is the Chobanid beylik until 1309 and Candar land afterwards (see the kastamonu dossier), so the successor is beylik-of-isfendiyar, which should list 'Kastamonu' in its cliopatria_names.

capitals.name: Sinop (Sinope)
capitals.note: Beyliks table: Pervâneid, capital Sinop, 1277-1322. The Candar page's infobox moves the Candar capital to Sinop only in 1398.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's row begins in 1305 but the beyliks table dates the Pervâneid state 1277-1322 (the Sinop page says independent emirates began after 1265). No page gives its extent before 1305; the 1305 shape stands in, approximate.

keyframe_review.note: Years only. 13,622 km2 along the Black Sea coast from the Sinop hinterland east towards Samsun (the Candar page lists Sinop and Samsun among the provinces the Candar realm eventually covered); neither page gives an area, so no infobox ratio. Cliopatria's row runs to 1332; the only dated end on a page opened is the table's 'Pervâneid ... Sinop ... 1277-1322'. The Candar page is silent on the year of annexation.

correction.text: no Sinop shape after 1322: the land is Candar territory from the 1322 annexation, drawn by the beylik-of-isfendiyar dossier (Candar realm; its cliopatria_names should include 'Kastamonu')

keyframe_review.note: The shape repeats 1305's for 1326-1332 although the Pervâneid state is dated 1277-1322 on the beyliks table; the Candar page has Süleyman I annex Sinop (reign 1309-1339), undated. Cliopatria shows the area passing to its Kastamonu row only in 1333. Relies on one table row: confidence 2.

ledger.note: 1277: the Pervâneid emirate at Sinop begins. Beyliks table: 'Pervâneid ... Sinop ... 1277-1322'; the Sinop page says that 'after 1265' the city became home to two successive independent emirates, the Pervâne and the Isfendiyars. The Candar page names the line only as 'the descendants of Mu'in al-Din Suleyman'.

region.text: Sinop, 'formerly ruled by the descendants of Mu'in al-Din Suleyman'

ledger.note: 1322: Süleyman I of the Candar dynasty annexes Sinop. The beyliks table ends the Pervâneid state in 1322; the Candar page says Süleyman I, once he had conquered Kastamonu, 'annexed Safranbolu and Sinop, formerly ruled by the descendants of Mu'in al-Din Suleyman' and made his son Ibrahim governor of Sinop, but gives no year. The Sinop page notes the bishop left Sinop in 1315 'because of the Isfendiyars', so the Candar pressure is older. Cliopatria's Kastamonu row absorbs the area only in 1333. The annexing Candar state is Cliopatria's Isfendiyar row (same article), so the counterpart is beylik-of-isfendiyar, not kastamonu (the Chobanid beylik, which ends in 1309).

1322: the Pervâneid emirate of Sinop ends (beyliks table 1277-1322); its land goes to the Candar state (beylik-of-isfendiyar), then seated at Kastamonu. The Pervâneoğlu page lists Gazi Çelebi, 'the last Bey of Pervane', as ruling 1300-1322 and says that, having no sons, he 'bequeathed his lands to the Candarids' (its overall range for the beylik is 1261-1326; its ruler table starts with Muînüddin Mehmed in 1277). Source added by the reviewer of me-09-f.

wars.name: Candarid annexation of Sinop
wars.outcome: Süleyman I of the Candars annexed Sinop and Safranbolu from the descendants of Mu'in al-Din Suleyman.
wars.note: Neither the Candar page nor the Sinop page dates any campaign; 1322 is the end of the Pervâneid state on the beyliks table. No contest is coded.

certainty.note: No page gives a boundary for the Pervâneid emirate; its inland limit towards Kastamonu and its eastern limit towards Trebizond's coast are approximate.

notes: Row identity: Cliopatria's 'Beylik of Sinop' (Wikipedia title 'Candar dynasty', Wikidata Q2096678, shared with beylik-of-isfendiyar) is, on the pages opened, the Pervâneid emirate of Sinop (descendants of Mu'in al-Din Suleyman), a different state from the Candars, who annexed it. It should not be merged with beylik-of-isfendiyar; the shared Wikidata id is the Candar dynasty article that Cliopatria attached to both rows. The Candar page treats Eflani/Kastamonu/Sinop as one realm of the Candar dynasty, so the colour agent may want beylik-of-isfendiyar and (after 1322) the Sinop land in one family; the Candar realm's Kastamonu province (from 1309) is carried by beylik-of-isfendiyar, and the kastamonu dossier is the Chobanid beylik only (1211-1309). A page on the Pervâneid line (Mu'in al-Din Suleyman and his descendants) was not found: the English Wikipedia titles tried failed (the reviewer of me-09-f found it at Pervâneoğlu: Gazi Çelebi 1300-1322 bequeathed his lands to the Candarids; added as the source of the 1322 dissolve). The end year 1322 rests on one table row (the small paraphrase of the Anatolian beyliks page); Cliopatria says 1332. The page budget (1-2 pages) was spent on Candar dynasty, Anatolian beyliks and Sinop.
